description:
Need to know if a website is down? Type its address and I’ll check it for you. 

I quickly test if the site can be reached and tell you what I find in clear, simple words. If the site is working, I’ll say it is online. If it is not working, I’ll explain that too. You do not need special computer skills. Just ask, and I’ll do the checking.

This is helpful when a page will not load, an app will not connect, or a service seems broken. Many problems look the same, but they can have different causes. A website may be down for everyone. It may only be blocked for you. Your internet may have a problem. The site may be slow. I help you understand what is most likely happening so you know what to try next.

Using me is easy. Tell me the website you want to check. You can paste a full web address or simply type the name of the site. I will test whether it can be reached and share the result in plain English. If there is useful extra information, I will explain what it means without lots of hard words.

You can check almost any public website. News sites, shops, games, schools, blogs, company pages, and online tools can all be checked. If a page is public on the internet, I can usually test whether it is responding. If a site cannot be checked for a technical reason, I will tell you instead of guessing.

If a website is online, I can help you think about why it still is not working for you. Maybe your browser needs to refresh. Maybe your internet connection has a problem. Maybe a VPN, firewall, or network setting is getting in the way. Sometimes waiting a few minutes is enough because a busy service starts working again.

If a website is down, I explain that in a simple way. I will not make up reasons or pretend to know something I cannot see. If there is not enough information, I will say so. Clear answers are better than confusing ones.

This tool is useful for everyone. Students can check school websites before class. Families can see if a favorite game or video site is having trouble. Workers can test company pages before reporting a problem. Developers can quickly check a public site before spending time looking for bugs. Support teams can use it as a fast first step when helping customers.

You can ask things like “Is this website down?”, “Can you check example.com?”, “Why won’t this page load?”, “Is the server online?”, or “Can anyone reach this site?” I understand many different ways of asking the same question, so you do not have to use special commands.

My goal is to save you time. Instead of trying many different things, start with a quick check. Knowing whether a website is online or offline helps you decide what to do next. That can stop wasted time, reduce worry, and make fixing problems much easier.

I focus on giving short, useful answers first. If you want more detail, just ask. I can explain what the result means, what you can try next, and which common problems might fit the situation. I keep the language simple, avoid unnecessary jargon, and stay honest about what I know.

Whether you are checking one website or many, I aim to make the process fast, clear, and easy. Paste a web address, type a site name, or ask if a service is down. I’ll check its reachability, explain the result, and help you understand what to do next.
